subject: Re: Next steps: Zenvera evaluation pilot & Redwood model recommendations
body:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenvera.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Zenvera evaluation pilot & Redwood model recommendations

Hi Sanjay / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Recap from our discovery and proposed next steps for the evaluation pilot on Redwood: V quick summary, then items for action.

Summary of ask
- Goal: replace rule-based triage for inbound patient messages with an LLM-assisted classification + suggested response feature.
- Primary KPIs: classification accuracy (macro-F1 > 0.83), average latency under 350ms p90, and maintain cost < $0.015 per inference for the 2k daily message baseline.

Redwood recommendations (initial)
- Candidate models to benchmark: Llama-2-13B (int8/quantized), Mistral-Instruct-7B (float16), and a smaller distilled variant (Redwood-small-3B) for latency-constrained routes.
- Embeddings: use semantic-qa embeddings for intent clustering (cosine), then pass top-k contexts to the generator. We recommend 1536-d embeddings (Open-embedding-1536 equivalent).
- Baseline: run your current rule-based output as the golden reference for classification scoring; include a held-out human-labeled set of ~1,000 examples.

Eval setup we propose (attached files):
- zenvera_sample_dataset.csv (attachment): columns: id, prompt, reference_label, category, metadata_json. Please use UTF-8, comma-separated.
- zenvera_eval_spec.md (attachment): includes scoring rubric, sample prompts for warmup, and instructions for generating variants.
- Scoring criteria: macro-F1 for classification; response quality scored 0-4 by human raters for a 500-sample subset; regression guardrail is any drop >3 points in human score vs. baseline.

Operational notes / guardrails
- Model pinning: for the pilot, we'll pin Llama-2-13B@v20270301 and Mistral-7B@v20270301 so we can compare deterministic snapshots.
- Regression monitoring: Redwood will run nightly evals and post a daily report to the Drive link below. If any model shows >5% latency increase or >3-point drop in human score, automatic fallback to Redwood-small-3B will trigger for the affected route.
- Privacy: all sample datasets stay in your VPC bucket during Private deployment; for hosted pilot we'll encrypt at rest and restrict access to the project team.

Next steps / asks for Zenvera
1) Share the exported sample CSV with ~1,500 mixed examples (you can include the rule-derived labels). Filename: zenvera_sample_dataset.csv.
2) Confirm which categories are critical vs optional (we flagged triage, escalation, billing).
3) Do you want Redwood to run the initial scoring and produce the human-rated subset, or will Zenvera provide human labels?

Timeline proposal
- You send dataset by Mon, Mar 15
- Redwood runs initial benchmark (3 models) and shares a result deck by Thu, Mar 18
- Follow-up call to review results week of Mar 22

\Attachments: zenvera_sample_dataset.csv (stub), zenvera_eval_spec.md (stub), redwood-model-recs.pdf (overview)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Vanessa and Ben for onboarding ops and scorer design.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
---

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenvera.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Zenvera evaluation pilot & Redwood model recommendations

Thanks Mateo — this looks great. A few clarifications:
- We do have a human-labeled holdout of ~600 messages from last quarter; is that sufficient for the human quality subset?
- Our infra team prefers the hosted pilot first (easier to iterate).
- Can Redwood assist with the human scoring rubric and recruit raters if needed?

Elena and I will push the dataset to the Drive link by Monday. One ask: on the CSV, we have nested JSON in metadata — is that okay or should we flatten?

— Sanjay
Head of Product, Zenvera Health

On Fri, Mar 12, 2027 at 08:42 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sanjay — great questions. Short answers: yes, 600 labeled examples is usable for a small human subset; we prefer 500+ for stable estimates but can proceed. Hosted pilot is fine.
> 
> For metadata: nested JSON is okay as long as it is contained in a single CSV cell and escaped properly (we recommend double-quoting the cell). The eval_spec.md includes a small script to parse and normalize.
> 
> We can run the human scoring for you — Redwood has a vetted rater pool and a scorer UI. If you want to own the labels, we’ll share the rubric and templates.
> 
> I’m looping Vanessa to coordinate onboarding, S3 share, and scoring setup.
> 
> Best,
> Mateo
> 

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@zenvera.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, Mar 12, 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Zenvera evaluation pilot & Redwood model recommendations

Hi Sanjay — welcome, and thanks for moving quickly. Operationally:
- I’ll create a scoped S3 bucket and a short-lived upload token for your export (if hosted). If you prefer Drive, share a folder and I’ll pull and validate.
- Ben will author the scorer instructions and run a calibration session with your SMEs. Ben, can you propose 3 time slots next week?

Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi all — available Tue 3/16 10–11 PT, Wed 3/17 2–3 PT, Thu 3/18 11–12 PT to run a 45-min calibration and rubric walk-through. I’ll attach the scorer template in the follow-up.
> 
> Quick note on models: to keep cost predictable we’ll configure batching and use prefix caching for repeated intents; I’ll include recommended batch sizes after I see sequence-length distribution.
> 
> -Ben
